profile_patterns.assessment: All learned profile patterns have a Tn5 motif as the top database match. The dominant learned matrices visually resemble the matched Tn5 patterns.

count_patterns.assessment: Dominant positive patterns are Tn5/enzyme-bias-like. Other matrices are predominantly diffuse GC-rich, AT-rich, or low-complexity effects rather than compact transcription-factor motifs.

residual_caveats: Count negative pattern 7 matches SP2 at q=2.93e-6 with 778 seqlets, but its learned matrix is a broad composition effect rather than a compact SP-family logo; it represents 1.97% of all count seqlets.
Count positive patterns 19 and 24 match ZN770 at low q-values but contain only 165 seqlets together (0.42% of all count seqlets) and visually show diffuse GC composition.
The full ChromBPNet no-bias model must be checked for residual Tn5 patterns and excessive GC-rich motifs. Revisit the bias threshold if the full model's leading motifs show systematic GC leakage.
decision: Use this bias model for the fold-0 full ChromBPNet pilot. This does not establish reliability of the full Muller-glia model and does not release differential accessibility.
